Yare
yah-RAY
v. (Hebrew)
Hebrew yārē’, “to fear, reverence, be in awe of.” The verb covers a range from terror (of an enemy or judgment) to reverent awe (of God, parents, holy things). The noun yir’ah is “fear, reverence”—the central component of the fear of the LORD.

📖 Biblical Definition

Yārē’ is the great Old Testament verb for fear, covering a semantic range from terror of an enemy or of judgment to the reverent awe of God Himself—and its supreme biblical use is in the phrase the fear of the LORD (yir’at YHWH), which the wisdom literature names as the beginning of wisdom, knowledge, and life. Proverbs 1:7: the fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction. Proverbs 9:10: the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding. Proverbs 14:27: the fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death. Proverbs 22:4: by humility and the fear of the LORD are riches, and honour, and life. Job 28:28: and unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding. Psalm 111:10: the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments. The fear of the LORD is therefore structurally foundational to biblical wisdom. It is the beginning—the entry-point; what precedes any genuine wisdom, knowledge, or understanding. It is the fountain of life—the source from which true life flows. It is the disposition of soul that takes God seriously, that treats His commandments as binding, that walks before Him with the reverence proper to a creature standing before its holy Maker. The biblical fear of the LORD is not the cringing terror of the slave before the tyrant (that is the fear sin produces in the soul that knows itself unforgiven), but the awed reverence of the son before the Father whose love and holiness together call forth the response. The two combine: God’s holiness produces awe; God’s love makes the awe filial; the saint in whom both operate fears the LORD with the reverence Scripture commends and the love Scripture commands. Christ Himself was a man of the fear of the LORD: Isaiah 11:2 prophesies that the Spirit of the LORD shall rest upon Him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, of counsel and might, of knowledge and of the fear of the LORD; and Isaiah 11:3, and shall make him of quick understanding in the fear of the LORD. The Lord Jesus, perfect Man, lived in the perfect fear of the LORD—the awed reverent love of the Father whose will He came to do. The saint’s sanctification is, in part, the recovery of this disposition: the fear of the LORD restored to its proper place as the beginning of wisdom and the fountain of life.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

(Hebrew term.) Yārē’: to fear, reverence, be in awe of; the great OT verb covering terror, reverent awe, and the central biblical category of the fear of the LORD (yir’at YHWH), which Proverbs names the beginning of wisdom, knowledge, and life.

FEAR, v.t. — 1. To feel a painful apprehension of some impending evil; to be afraid of. 2. To reverence; to have a reverential awe; to venerate. The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom (Ps 111:10).

YARE — (Hebrew verb, H3372.) To fear, reverence; over 300 OT uses. Cognate noun yir’ah (H3374), fear, reverence; especially in yir’at YHWH, the fear of the LORD.

📖 Key Scripture

Proverbs 1:7 — "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction."

Proverbs 9:10 — "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding."

Proverbs 14:27 — "The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death."

Isaiah 11:2-3 — "And the spirit of the LORD shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the LORD; And shall make him of quick understanding in the fear of the LORD."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Yārē’-shaped fear of the LORD is corrupted, in the contemporary church, by the systematic flattening of fear into respect—a translation move that empties the awe-component that Scripture insists upon—and by the inverse corruption that mistakes biblical fear of the LORD for the cringing terror of the slave, which is precisely what regenerate sons of the Father do not experience.

expand to see more

The systematic flattening of fear into respect is the most pervasive contemporary corruption. Modern translations and sermons regularly render fear of the LORD as reverence for the LORD or respect for the LORD, on the reasonable ground that fear in modern English has acquired primarily a terror-of-harm sense that does not capture the biblical category. The trade is real but costly. The biblical yir’at YHWH includes reverence and respect but is not exhausted by them; it carries an awe-component that recognizes the holiness, the majesty, the judgment-capacity, the unmediated weight of the holy God Himself. The believer who has been taught only respect for the LORD has not encountered the doctrine Proverbs names as the beginning of wisdom. The recovery is the substantial doctrine of God in His holiness: where God is preached and worshipped in His holiness, the fear of the LORD returns of itself, including its awe-component, including the proper trembling Scripture commends (him that trembleth at my word, Isa 66:2), without slipping into the cringing terror of the unforgiven.

The opposite corruption is the mistaking of biblical fear of the LORD for the cringing terror of the slave. The believer is taught that God is love and that perfect love casts out fear (1 John 4:18), and concludes that any fear of God in the regenerate is sub-Christian, a residue of legalism, a failure to grasp the gospel. The text Scripture actually gives is more nuanced. 1 John 4:18 contrasts perfect love with the fear that hath torment—the cringing terror of the soul that expects punishment—and announces that perfect love casts that fear out. It does not abolish the fear of the LORD that Scripture elsewhere commends as the beginning of wisdom; it abolishes the slavish terror of the unforgiven and replaces it with the filial reverence of the adopted son. The Father is to be feared with the awed love of the regenerate; the tyrant is to be feared with the cringing terror of the slave. The biblical pattern is the first, not the second; the contemporary church often loses both, leaving the believer with neither the proper awe nor the proper assurance. Recover both. Refuse the flattening that empties the fear of the LORD of its awe-component, and refuse the cringing slavish terror that the gospel has freed the saint from. The biblical fear of the LORD is the awed reverent love of the Father, the beginning of wisdom, the fountain of life—and the church saturated with it is the church whose worship has the seriousness, and whose discipleship has the substance, that the loss of the fear of the LORD has, in much of the contemporary church, quietly drained.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew yārē’ (to fear, reverence, be in awe), with cognate noun yir’ah (fear)—the great OT verb of the awed reverent love of God that Proverbs names the beginning of wisdom and the fountain of life, fulfilled in Christ on whom the Spirit of the fear of the LORD rests (Isa 11:2-3).

expand to see more

Hebrew yārē’ (H3372) — to fear, reverence (over 300 OT uses).

Hebrew yir’ah (H3374) — fear, reverence (the cognate noun, especially in yir’at YHWH).

Hebrew pachad (H6342) — to dread, be in dread (the cousin verb for dread/terror).

Greek phobos (G5401) — fear, reverence (the NT cousin term).

Usage

"The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge—Proverbs sets yir’at YHWH as the entry-point of all genuine wisdom."

"Biblical fear of the LORD is the awed reverent love of the Father, not the cringing terror of the slave; perfect love casts out the latter and produces the former."

"Contemporary translation flattens fear into respect (losing the awe); contemporary preaching mistakes biblical fear for slavish terror (losing the doctrine entirely); recovery is the substantive doctrine of God in His holiness, which produces the fear of the LORD of itself."
